subject: journey/nautilus
prompt: Use case: illustration-story. A single landscape 3:2 illustration for the historical atlas sketchbook of Jules Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea. A nineteenth-century naturalist's field sketch in graphite and sepia pen with restrained transparent watercolour washes on warm ivory paper. Fine irregular parallel hatching, economical contour lines, a few details sharply observed; leave areas of cream paper around irregular unfinished edges. One coherent scene that reads at small sizes. No captions, labels, border, binding, signatures, photorealism, modern equipment, or Disney submarine designs. Quiet close water-level study of a living solitary dugong surfacing in the nineteenth-century Red Sea near Jeddah. The broad downturned whiskered muzzle breaks the surface to breathe; one curved flipper and a faint crescent tail visible under clear green water. No hunters or injuries.
